nodes.title: GWAS summary-stat files are often not sorted by position within a chromosome
nodes.summary: A GWAS parser that assumes sorted-by-position streaming will silently misassign SNPs to the wrong interval/locus when the input isn't actually sorted that way -- which is common for real GWAS files. Use an interval lookup structure instead of a sorted-streaming assumption so SNPs are assigned correctly regardless of file order.
nodes.trigger: writing a new parser that reads a GWAS summary-statistics file and assigns SNPs to loci/regions by position

nodes.title: Fingerprint-based staleness check to skip unnecessary reprocessing
nodes.summary: Hash the input file(s) + the relevant config + the pipeline/tool version together into one fingerprint per output; only reprocess when the fingerprint changes. Avoids rerunning expensive steps when nothing that could affect the output has actually changed, without needing a full dependency-graph system.

nodes.title: JSONP-wrapped static JSON files for CORS-free local-filesystem serving
nodes.summary: When a browser-based viewer needs to load many small per-item JSON files directly from the local filesystem (file:// URLs, no server), wrap each JSON payload in a JS function call (e.g. `loadLocus123({...})`) and load it via a <script> tag instead of fetch()/XHR -- script tags aren't subject to the same-origin/CORS restrictions that block local-file fetch() calls.
nodes.trigger: building a browser viewer that needs to load many separate JSON data files without running a server

nodes.title: Java `static final int` port constants get inlined — recompiling one file won't change other classes' printed values
nodes.summary: LocalServer.PORT is `public static final int PORT = 8765`, a compile-time constant. Recompiling only LocalServer.java with a new value (e.g. to test on a second port without touching the live server) correctly changes LocalServer's own runtime bind (InetSocketAddress uses the fresh value), but any other already-compiled class that references LocalServer.PORT (e.g. Main.java's startup printf) keeps the OLD value baked in at its call sites, because javac inlines static final primitive/String constants everywhere they're referenced, not just where they're declared. Symptom: the console log says 'Server at http://localhost:8765/' even though netstat shows it's actually listening on 8766. Verify the real bound port with netstat/ss, not by trusting printed log text, whenever only a subset of classes was recompiled.
nodes.trigger: Testing a Java app that hardcodes a port/value as `static final`, by recompiling just one file into a copied bin/ to run a second instance on a different port for verification.

nodes.title: LYNXgwas: raw GWAS input files get deleted post-processing, but .gz originals survive as siblings
nodes.summary: In this environment's fully-processed demo corpus (scz-full-demo/workspace and disease-demos/), each project's config.properties gwas.file points at a decompressed .tsv/.txt that no longer exists on disk (deleted after the earlier full-reprocessing pass to save space) — but a same-named .tsv.gz/.txt.gz sibling is still present one directory over (e.g. disease-demos/scz_extra/, disease-demos/t2d/, disease-demos/cad/, and scz-full-demo/PGC3_SCZ_full.tsv.gz). MultiLocusMerger/MultiLocusScanner (and presumably the single-project pipeline) read cfg.gwasFile directly and fail with a bare 'file not found' if only the .gz exists. Fix: `gunzip -k -f <the>.gz` to restore the exact decompressed filename the config expects, without touching/deleting the .gz. Needed before any locus-matrix / gene-constellation / multi-dataset run against 'already processed' projects in this corpus can actually execute for real (rather than replaying only previously-cached merged.tsv outputs).
nodes.trigger: A locus-matrix/gene-constellation (or any multi-project merge) run against the scz-full-demo / disease-demos corpus fails with '<file>.tsv (The system cannot find the file specified)'.

nodes.title: Unlifted genome build silently drops GWAS loci instead of erroring
nodes.summary: A summary-stats dataset left on hg18 in a GRCh37 pipeline (GRCh37 LD reference, GRCh37 GFF3) processed 'successfully' but found only 3 loci; after liftover to GRCh37 the same data gave 8 loci matching the published paper.
nodes.detail: Position-matched joins against the reference panel just lose SNPs, so there's no crash, only fewer and weaker loci. Check genome.build for every input before cross-dataset comparisons, and lift with a chain file (pyliftover), keeping only unique same-chromosome mappings and complementing alleles on '-' strand hits.
nodes.trigger: combining GWAS summary stats from different studies or eras (hg18/GRCh37/GRCh38) into one pipeline

nodes.title: Fast parallel liftover of 50M-row METAL output with pyliftover
nodes.summary: Stream the table in 2M-row pandas chunks through a multiprocessing Pool (each worker loads the chain once in its initializer). About 280 s for 52M variants on 12 workers.
nodes.detail: Per chunk: drop unwanted single-cohort variants via the METAL Direction column (e.g. '??x' = only the 3rd cohort), convert chr:pos to 0-based for convert_coordinate, keep len(result)==1 and same chrom, complement alleles on '-' strand, then do a global dedup on chrom:pos:alleles keeping the min p. Infer the Direction column's cohort order from the METAL Weight column (= that cohort's N when only one cohort is present).
nodes.snippet:
with Pool(12, initializer=init) as pool:
    for res, st in pool.imap(work, pd.read_csv(SRC, sep='	', chunksize=2_000_000)): parts.append(res)

nodes.title: Windows PowerShell 5.1 Get-Content/Set-Content silently mojibakes UTF-8 files
nodes.summary: Editing a BOM-less UTF-8 file with (Get-Content -Raw) -replace ... | Set-Content -Encoding utf8 reads it as cp1252, so every non-ASCII character (—, ×, ⁻, ≥) was turned into mojibake (â€” etc.) across a whole HTML page.
nodes.detail: Fix: re-encode each char as cp1252 (map chars undefined in cp1252, like U+0081, back to their single byte), then decode as UTF-8. Prevention: never round-trip UTF-8 source through PowerShell 5.1 cmdlets; use Python with explicit encoding='utf-8' or the Edit tool.
nodes.trigger: making a quick text replacement in a UTF-8 file from PowerShell on Windows

nodes.title: Sparse-profile outliers hijack hierarchical-cluster count selection
nodes.summary: Clustering GWAS datasets by locus-significance profiles: datasets with ~0 significant loci sit at cosine distance ~1 from everything, so the silhouette picks K=2 (outlier vs rest) and a fixed-K cut spends clusters on singletons. Excluding datasets with <3 genome-wide significant loci (still displayed and reported) took ARI vs disease from 0.00 to 0.70 on a 31-dataset corpus.
nodes.detail: Check a cluster-count rule on the real matrix in scipy/sklearn before hard-coding it. A synthetic test with injected zero-signal outliers caught the first rule failing.

nodes.title: PLINK 1.9 reserves half of RAM per process: parallel runs silently OOM and look like 'no variants'
nodes.summary: Without --memory, every PLINK 1.9 process reserves ~50% of physical RAM. Running several in parallel (plus a JVM heap) makes some exit with 'Error: Out of memory' before writing output; code that discards PLINK output then reports a misleading downstream error (e.g. 'No ref panel variants in locus region', 'matched_ref.bim not found').
nodes.detail: Seen in LYNXgwas base build: 6 parallel locus builds on a 32 GB machine with a 12 GB JVM -> ~240/1637 loci failed; the same loci succeeded serially. Scanning a 46M-variant reference .bim with --chr/--from-bp needs ~3 GB (2 GB fails, 3 GB works). Fix: pass explicit --memory (4096 for full-panel scans, 2048 for small subsets) and --threads 1, gate concurrent PLINK memory with a shared semaphore budget (physical RAM - JVM max heap - reserve), and keep PLINK's output tail for error messages. Also: PLINK exit 12 'All variants excluded' just means the region is empty in the panel (e.g. chrX in an autosome-only panel). And make step caches verify their actual output files exist, not just a manifest, or a failed run's manifest poisons reruns.
nodes.trigger: Running many PLINK 1.9 jobs concurrently (threads/snakemake/parallel loci) and a subset of them fail with empty/missing outputs or 'no variants' errors that disappear when rerun serially

nodes.title: bigsnpr::snp_cor is windowed (500 SNPs) by default: invalid LD for SuSiE on wide loci, and nearPD takes tens of minutes
nodes.summary: snp_cor(Gna, ind.col) only correlates SNPs within size=500 positions and stores 0 elsewhere. For fine-mapping windows >500 SNPs the result is not a valid correlation matrix (hundreds of negative eigenvalues, min ~ -15), so a nearPD repair runs ~20 s per iteration for up to 100 iterations, and distant-pair LD is wrong. Pass size=length(ind.col) to get the full matrix (PSD; 3 s for 2,400 SNPs; SuSiE then 3 s).
nodes.detail: Found running SuSiE on 1,600 GWAS loci through LYNXgwas: 3 min/locus with 3 in parallel; profiling showed susie_rss itself is 0.4 s and nearPD the bottleneck. Also: identify monomorphic SNPs by snp_MAF(G, ind.col) == 0 (NaN row counting fails with a windowed/sparse matrix), use ncores=1 when running loci in parallel, and judge credible-set purity on the unshrunk LD (shrinking R by lambda scales correlations by 1-lambda and drops sets just above min_abs_corr=0.5).
nodes.trigger: SuSiE-RSS with a bigsnpr LD matrix is very slow, needs nearPD, reports many negative eigenvalues, or loses credible sets on wide loci

nodes.title: Build scripts that rm -rf their output dir must refuse when it holds a live deployment (settings, junctions to data)
nodes.summary: A packaging script that recreated dist/<name> with rm -rf wiped a test deployment living in that folder (server.properties, junctions to 21 GB of datasets). Git Bash rm -rf removed the junctions without following them, so the data survived, but that is not guaranteed across tools. Guard: abort if the output folder contains live config or non-empty data dirs.
nodes.detail: lynxgwas-server/scripts/package-server.sh now exits 3 when $OUT/server.properties exists or $OUT/app/projects is non-empty. Keep live deployments outside build output dirs; keep server state (accounts, keys) outside the package too (data.dir), which is why accounts survived.
nodes.trigger: A build/package script deletes and recreates an output directory that someone may also run the app from

nodes.title: Estimate mvSuSiE residual (sample-overlap) correlation from genome-wide null SNPs, not the locus window
nodes.summary: Null-z correlation computed from |z|<2 SNPs inside a strong locus window is inflated by shared true signal leaking via LD (e.g. CAD pairs 0.6-0.86 vs 0.36-0.58 genome-wide; cross-disease 0.1-0.4 vs ~0). Feeding that V to mvsusie_rss splits one shared signal into many dataset-specific single-SNP credible sets (ATXN2/SH2B3: 10 sets -> 1 set led by rs3184504 active in all 10 datasets after the fix). Also: requiring SNPs null in ALL K datasets leaves too few SNPs (44 for K=10) and silently falls back to identity, hiding overlap.
nodes.detail: Fix: per dataset, thin the full GWAS file deterministically (pos %% 53 == 7, ~2%), orient z to a strand-collapsed alphabetical allele, drop palindromic, cache; estimate V pairwise over SNPs on other chromosomes with |z|<2 in both, require >=1000 SNPs per pair.
nodes.trigger: building the residual_variance / V matrix for mvSuSiE, MTAG, or any multi-GWAS joint model

nodes.title: Git Bash: /tmp paths inside a ;-separated Java classpath are not translated
nodes.summary: MSYS converts a standalone /tmp/x argument (javac -d /tmp/x works) but not one embedded in "/tmp/x;bin;lib/*", so java silently falls through to stale classes later on the classpath (old test classes in bin/ ran and 'passed'). Use $(cygpath -w /tmp/x) in the classpath.
nodes.trigger: running java with a mixed classpath from Git Bash on Windows

nodes.title: Separate crowded 1-D tracks (serpents, labels) with least-squares block merging, and fall back when too crowded
nodes.summary: Sort items by true x; each item has its own left/right reach (e.g. max sideways drift + half ribbon width). Required gap between neighbours = right reach of left + left reach of right + margin. Push items into blocks: when a new block collides with the previous, merge and place the merged block at the mean of (desired x - offset within block), repeat while collisions remain; clamp blocks to the axis. Draw each item from its true position on the axis and let it bend into its lane. If the total required width exceeds ~1/0.6 of the axis, skip the layout entirely: spreading everything evenly creates long diagonal leaders that are worse than overlap; tell the user to zoom instead.

nodes.title: Bash tool heredocs can collapse \ before Python sees it: put edit scripts with escapes in files
nodes.summary: In this environment a python heredoc (<<'EOF') string containing — or \" reached Python as — -> a real em-dash, so an exact-match replace silently failed to match (assert count==1 caught it). For edits whose search/replace text contains backslashes (JS unicode escapes, Java string escapes), write the edit script with the Write tool and use raw strings, then run it.
nodes.trigger: scripted find/replace edits whose text contains backslashes
